AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2 (monster stream), copied verbatim per governing rule 3 and not re-derived. The sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation *is* construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (mecha_knight.py:32-36). Same observable today, established by execution rather than assumed, on all three clauses: (a) listener set -- the only ported listeners on the hooks a starting power can reach are relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38 and relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53 (modify_power_amount) and relics/vambrace.py:26-40 / relics/paels_legion.py:36-43 (modify_block_multiplicative); all four gate on `target is self.player` / `applier is self.player` / `card is not None`, and a monster's starting power is self-applied with no card, so none of them can fire. sts2_rl/potions.py implements none of the four hooks. (b) HP-roll inversion -- the sim applies the power before the Niche roll and the game after it; of the 35 constructor-applied power classes only IllusionPower mentions max_hp at all and only inside revive() (powers.py:1581), never at apply time. (c) roll ordering -- MachineMonster.__init__ rolls the first move (state_machine.py:301) *before* the subclass applies its powers, and `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py roll-order` shows all 29 machine sites are sticky-no-op: this unit's initial state is a MoveState, so monster_state_machine step 30's early return fires and the first roll evaluates no branch and reads no power. Concrete trigger that would make it a gap: any relic, potion or power that listens on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. RULE 7: the four relic files and powers.py cited above are NOT hashed by this record (powers.py IS hashed here for other entries); flagged explicitly as the shared finding instructs. ESCALATION CHECK: MechaKnight.cs:73-77 applies ArtifactPower 3m to itself and nothing else; _ARTIFACT = 3 (mecha_knight.py:18). Artifact is the one starting power in this batch that INTERCEPTS later applications (cmds.py:299-306 decrements it and returns before the debuff lands), so the apply-order inversion deserves the check rather than a blind copy -- but the inversion is only relative to the Niche HP roll and the relic/potion attach, all of which happen before the first player action, and no debuff can reach the Mecha Knight before combat starts. Clause (c) holds: the initial state is the MoveState CHARGE_MOVE, so the constructor roll is a sticky no-op.

GenerateAnimator.rationale: Presentation only, per SHARED-FINDINGS section 4 (monster stream) and monster_state_machine guards N2/N5. This is the animator that reads IsWoundUp -- 14 conditional AddBranch("Hit", ...) edges picking hurt vs hurt_wound (MechaKnight.cs:162-175). Note these are CreatureAnimator.AddBranch(string, ...), a different overload family from RandomBranchState.AddBranch, and monster_state_machine's 61-site census explicitly subtracts them; no state-machine integer is involved.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Node-by-node against MechaKnight.cs:79-95. Four MoveStates with matching ids (CHARGE_MOVE / FLAMETHROWER_MOVE / WINDUP_MOVE / HEAVY_CLEAVE_MOVE) and the same chain CHARGE -> FLAMETHROWER -> WINDUP -> HEAVY_CLEAVE -> FLAMETHROWER (MechaKnight.cs:86-89 vs mecha_knight.py:53-56), so CHARGE fires once and the tail is a three-cycle. INITIAL state CHARGE_MOVE on both (:94 vs :58). The C# `list` is built in a different ORDER from the sim's ([charge, cleave, windup, flamethrower] vs the sim's identical [charge, heavy_cleave, windup, flamethrower]) -- and in any case the list is only a registration bag: RegisterStates adds each state to a dict by id (monster_state_machine step 23), and no walk iterates it. No branch state, so no AddBranch integer and no MonsterAi draw.

guards.rationale: ChargeDamage GetValueIfAscension(DeadlyEnemies, 30, 25) -> 25; HeavyCleaveDamage (..., 40, 35) -> 35; WindupMove gains 15m block with ValueProp.Move then applies StrengthPower 5m to itself (MechaKnight.cs:128-129). All match mecha_knight.py:13-18 and the handlers at :61-78, including the block-BEFORE-Strength order in _windup (:74-75), which matters because a later ModifyBlock listener keyed on Strength would see a different value if the two were swapped.

guards.what: FlamethrowerMove adds 4 Burn to HAND (MechaKnight.cs:136 vs mecha_knight.py:64-68)
guards.rationale: C# is `CardPileCmd.AddToCombatAndPreview<Burn>(targets, PileType.Hand, 4, null)` with the default CardPilePosition.Bottom; the sim loops add_to_hand four times. Card count and pile match. Two guards C# carries that the sim expresses differently, both checked: (1) `if (player.Creature.IsDead) return` (CardPileCmd.cs:1008-1011) -- the sim has no such check, but a dead player ends the combat before any later reader can see the hand, so nothing observable differs; (2) hand overflow -- the sim routes the 4th..Nth card to the discard when the hand is at MAX_HAND_SIZE (cmds.py:508-511), which is the ported convention that creature_card_cmds already owns. The `_flamethrowerCardCount = 4` const (MechaKnight.cs:28) agrees with both the call and the intent.

guards.what: StatusIntent(4)'s CardCount is dropped by the sim's Intent (MechaKnight.cs:83 vs mecha_knight.py:42-44)
guards.rationale: Presentation only, per SHARED-FINDINGS section 4 (monster stream) and monster_state_machine guards N2/N5. Same mechanism and same verdict as monster/noisebot's guard (governing rule 3): StatusIntent.CardCount is read only by GetIntentLabel and GetIntentDescription in StatusIntent.cs, both of which only fill a LocString for the intent tooltip, and `grep -rn CardCount src/` finds no other consumer. No sim consumer of Intent reads a status count either (env.py:167 and full_env.py:571 are booleans). The 4 cards actually added are correct.

guards.what: IsWoundUp (MechaKnight.cs:38, 60-71, 109, 125) is dropped by the port
guards.rationale: Presentation only, per SHARED-FINDINGS section 4 (monster stream) and monster_state_machine guards N2/N5. Read to the END before deciding, per KinPriest N6: the property is set true in WindupMove and false in HeavyCleaveMove, and its ONLY readers are the 14 conditional animator edges at MechaKnight.cs:162-175 that choose the wound-up idle/hurt animations. No move, no branch and no damage number consults it, so a port that drops the flag loses nothing mechanical.
